messages.author: 048d1222bb0af667
messages.subject: How to analise model convergence
parts:
Hello, everyone!

I'm really enjoying using INLA for my thesis but now I'm having difficulties on how to analise model convergence, namely doing trace and density plots and evaluating the values of Gelman and Rubin's estimate, R hat.

Is this possible or something similiar to do in inla?

Thank you all
Ema Biscaia

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How to analise model convergence
parts:
thx Ema! there is no MCMC so no trace-plots to look at. You can read
about the background of INLA in the 2009 paper or one of the review
papers

messages.author: 5f37ffd5fb192336
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How to analise model convergence
parts:
Hi Ema, 

INLAjoint cannot fit spatial survival models (as you know based on our correspondence).

But as with all Bayesian models the basics hold:
Are the posteriors unimodal? 
Are the posteriors different from the priors?
Do the predicted survival probabilities make sense?
etc...

These things are not software specific and should always be checked no matter what you use to perform the Bayesian inference.
